facility: Chaohu, Anhui; Wutai, Shanxi; associate Anhui Baomei at Qingyang; Gansu Baomei supplies ferrosilicon
raw_feedstock: Dolomite; ferrosilicon reductant and alloy additions. Raw carbonate rock is distinct from calcined dolime entering the reduction blend.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Controlled dolomite resources: Chaohu about 90 million t, Wutai 580 million t; associate Baomei at Qingyang about 1.3 billion t. H1 2026 report confirms Chaohu mining, while Wutai mine safety-design approval was still progressing. These are resource holdings, not annual feed. Gansu’s approximately 14 million t quartz resource supports the silicon/ferrosilicon chain, not the magnesium mineral input. The first furnace of Gansu Baomei’s planned 300,000 t/y FeSi project started in May 2026, prioritizing internal Mg plants. Purchased suppliers remain unnamed.
prepared_feed_and_route: Mine and crush dolomite → calcine to dolime and prepare a ferrosilicon-bearing charge → vacuum silicothermic reduction using the group’s vertical-retort technology → condense/refine magnesium → sell ingot/alloy or consume it in component production. The filing describes the group route; a plant-by-plant technology allocation is not given.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No facility-linked dolomite MgO/Mg assay, impurity analysis or prepared-charge specification located. Resource tonnage does not establish metallurgical grade.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No disclosed plant-boundary t dry dolomite/t primary Mg or reductant consumption found.
supply_constraints: Wutai mine approvals and Gansu FeSi ramp-up constrain how resource ownership can be interpreted as available captive supply. The full FeSi project nameplate is not the capacity of the first commissioned furnace. Qingyang mining was partly developed in January 2026.

facility: Fugu / Laogaochuan, Shaanxi; Tianyu and related Xiyuan operations
raw_feedstock: Dolomite, ferrosilicon and fuel gas associated with the coal/semi-coke complex.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Fugu industrial cluster. Specific dolomite quarry, current supplier and proportion of internally supplied ferrosilicon are undisclosed. Do not treat regional coal mining as magnesium mineral supply.
prepared_feed_and_route: Dolomite preparation and calcination → dolime/ferrosilicon charge → silicothermic magnesium production → refining and alloy casting. Commercial integration is documented; a current facility process audit was not located.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No source-matched ore or calcined-feed assay located; no numerical impurities disclosed.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No annual mine-to-metal or charge-to-metal mass balance located.
supply_constraints: The chairman described dolomite mining restrictions, transport and ferrosilicon availability/cost constraints in 2019. These are historical dependencies, not proof of current interruption.

facility: Wenxi, Shanxi; Yinguang Huasheng and related group facilities
raw_feedstock: Dolomite for primary metal; ferrosilicon reductant; primary metal then enters the alloy/fabrication chain.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Company describes integrated mineral-to-metal operations in Wenxi. Exact quarry, annual mine draw and external purchase share not disclosed in reviewed material.
prepared_feed_and_route: Dolomite → calcined feed → thermal reduction → crude metal refining/alloying → wrought/forged products. Integrated operations are supported, but a current Huasheng-specific reduction specification was not found; this route is a synthesis rather than an equipment-level verification.
grade_and_analytical_basis: Dolomite MgO content, moisture basis, silica/iron limits and prepared blend grade are undisclosed.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No documented feed-to-primary-metal ratio found.
supply_constraints: No facility-specific current feed disruption established; mining and smelting integration does not eliminate reductant and energy dependencies.

raw_feedstock: Dolomite from an associated mine; calcined dolomite is the prepared mineral feed. Reductant sourcing is not detailed.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Company claims a dolomite mine about 8 km from the plant and resources around 200 million t. This supports captive provenance; no current mine output or audited reserve classification provided.
prepared_feed_and_route: Dolomite quarrying/preparation → calcination and thermal reduction → refining/alloying → ingots and cast components. The mineral-to-product chain is described commercially; current retort configuration is not verified.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No numerical feed assay or impurity limits located. Advertised high purity must not be converted into a numerical ore grade.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No supported dolomite or reductant consumption per tonne of metal.
supply_constraints: Captive nearby mineral source is documented; current external reductant and energy supply terms are undisclosed.

raw_feedstock: Dolomite-based regional thermal route; ferrosilicon and fuel required. Plant-specific mineral contract not located.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Fugu location documented; exact quarry/supplier and internal-versus-purchased feed split unknown.
prepared_feed_and_route: A February 2026 Fugu report identifies a Jinwantong silicothermic Mg99.95A demonstration line in stable trial operation. In this thermal route, prepared oxide feed is reduced with a silicon-bearing charge, then metal is condensed/refined. The site’s full feed-preparation specification and other-line status remain unverified.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No feed or prepared-charge assay located. Mg99.95A is a final-product designation in the demonstration report, not a feed assay.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No documented feed-to-metal ratio.
supply_constraints: March 2026 maintenance affected a reported 120 t/day rate; it is not multiplied by 365. A completed restart was not verified.

raw_feedstock: Dolomite; ferrosilicon; small fluorite addition. Dolomite is first calcined, then ground and briquetted with the reductant.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Dolomite quarry/supplier undisclosed. Site has 10,000 t/y ferrosilicon and 300,000 t/y semi-coke capacities; these establish integration, not proof that all reductant is internally supplied.
prepared_feed_and_route: Calcine dolomite → grind with ferrosilicon and a small fluorite addition → briquette → Pidgeon vacuum reduction → refine crude magnesium and cast saleable ingot. This route is explicitly described for this facility.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No feed MgO assay or impurity limits provided. Reported grade-one/grade-two product proportions are product classification yields, not ore recovery.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No t dolomite/t Mg or reductant consumption disclosed.
supply_constraints: Documented industrial integration links production to ferrosilicon and semi-coke operations; no specific supply interruption established.

facility: Historical Ningxia operation; successor facility boundary unresolved
raw_feedstock: Mineral and purchased-intermediate details not established by reviewed company-specific sources.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Mine, supplier and internal sourcing share undisclosed in reviewed evidence.
prepared_feed_and_route: Historical producer table establishes primary metal output, but does not verify the facility’s present production route. A China-wide Pidgeon assumption is not promoted to a plant-specific fact.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No feed or prepared-material assays located.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No ratio disclosed.
supply_constraints: Bankruptcy liquidation prevents treating the historical corporate capacity as confirmed current supply. Successor operating arrangements have not been verified.

facility: Group bases in Shanxi and Shandong; primary-smelter allocation unresolved
raw_feedstock: No sufficiently sourced facility-level raw-feed/purchased-intermediate inventory located.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Mine or supplier provenance and captive/purchased split remain unknown.
prepared_feed_and_route: Identified in producer statistics, but facility-specific operating process not verified in reviewed sources. Regional thermal production is context only.
grade_and_analytical_basis: Feed grade, impurities and prepared-feed specification undisclosed.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No feed-to-product ratio located.
supply_constraints: No company-specific supply constraint established.

facility: Xinjiang Tengxiang, Hami; Baishan Tianan, Jilin
raw_feedstock: Dolomite for thermal production; ferrosilicon reductant. Hami energy integration relies on semi-coke gas.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Baishan circular describes a captive dolomite mine about 12 km from the plant, historical mining capacity 450,000 t/y and 23.027 million t resource as of 2009. These facts do not establish feed to Hami, whose quarry source is undisclosed.
prepared_feed_and_route: Historical dolomite calcination → thermal reduction → refining/alloy production. During Hami upgrades the group plans trading and commissioned processing; purchased finished metal/alloy is therefore distinct from its own primary production. Baishan’s newly commercial ore-powder line is not a magnesium smelter.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No mine-specific MgO/Mg assay or prepared-charge impurity analysis verified.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: Mine capacity is not feed consumption; no defensible t ore/t Mg ratio.
supply_constraints: Hami environmental rectification requires semi-coke facilities to be upgraded; financing constraints prompted suspension arrangements. Current restart date unverified.

raw_feedstock: Dead Sea brine is the raw resource. Carnallite recovered by the integrated Dead Sea Works evaporation system is the magnesium-rich intermediate; the electrolyser requires prepared, dehydrated chloride feed.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Internally integrated supply from the northern Dead Sea basin through Dead Sea Works ponds and carnallite harvesting. No outside mine is required for this principal magnesium feed.
prepared_feed_and_route: Evaporate brine and harvest carnallite → prepare/dehydrate chloride salts → VAMI-type molten-salt electrolysis → refine magnesium and alloy/cast saleable metal. Chlorine participates in the wider integrated chemical complex.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No current plant feed Mg concentration or impurity specification located. ICL’s approximately 20% KCl figure describes harvested potash-bearing material, not elemental Mg grade.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No public, boundary-consistent brine-volume or carnallite-mass consumption per tonne of magnesium found.
supply_constraints: Continuous power, pond salt harvesting and reliable brine access underpin production. Concession expiry in 2030 and regional logistics/security are disclosed risks.

raw_feedstock: Dolomite plus ferrosilicon. Prepared reduction mix reported as about 85% calcined dolomite and 15% ferrosilicon; reductant contains about 75% Si. Quartz, charcoal and iron-bearing materials used for ferrosilicon are auxiliary upstream inputs, not magnesium ore.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Company reports its own high-purity dolomite supply; exact mine name and numerical assay were not located. Ferrosilicon is produced within RIMA’s integrated operations.
prepared_feed_and_route: Calcine dolomite → grind/briquette the oxide feed with ferrosilicon and silicon reductants → proprietary RIMA vacuum silicothermic reduction → condense magnesium crystals → refine and cast ingot/alloy, make powder or feed component production. SECEX’s September 2026 description of Bocaiúva specifies internal heating around 1,200 °C for approximately 10 hours before crystal recovery, with heat recovery between charge columns. These are described process conditions, not an annual throughput or recovery guarantee.
grade_and_analytical_basis: Dolomite assay undisclosed. The 75% Si figure is reductant composition; minimum 99.8% Mg refers to saleable raw metal, not ore.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: 85:15 is prepared-charge mass composition; it is not 85 t ore per 15 t metal and does not yield a mine-to-metal consumption factor. No such factor disclosed. The same notice reverses the respective percentages in stage iv; the explicit 85% dolime / 15% FeSi statement comes from stage i.
supply_constraints: Captive mineral/reductant integration is documented. Government review identifies RIMA as the entire domestic primary raw-magnesium industry for Apr 2025–Mar 2026, but withholds production tonnage.

raw_feedstock: Carnallite chloride mineral; dried/dehydrated salt is the prepared electrolysis feed.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Historical supply from Uralkali’s Verkhnekamskoye carnallite operations. Uralkali’s 2024 report confirms Solikamsk-1 carnallite mining/processing, but a present SMZ purchase contract was not found. Feed is historically purchased, not a demonstrated SMZ-owned mine.
prepared_feed_and_route: Prepare/dehydrate carnallite → molten-salt electrolysis → refine and cast magnesium/alloys. Chlorine supports the integrated chemical chain. Company confirms electrolytic magnesium manufacture. A February 2026 company repair announcement confirms carnallite dehydration within the magnesium-electrolysis department.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No current contracted raw-carnallite assay or electrolyser-feed impurity specification verified.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No annual feed-to-metal consumption boundary located; co-production of chlorine complicates allocation.
supply_constraints: SMM reported equipment upgrades constraining output in March 2026. Its monthly signal is not annualized. Historical dependence on external carnallite remains a supply-chain consideration, not proof of current shortage.

raw_feedstock: Purchased/prepared carnallite feed and internally returned MgCl2 from titanium reduction. Virgin mineral input and recycled chloride are separate magnesium sources.
source_and_purchase_boundary: External carnallite mine/supplier not disclosed in the reviewed technical reference. Titanium mineral resources cannot be substituted as the source of magnesium. Internal MgCl2 arises when magnesium reduces titanium chloride.
prepared_feed_and_route: Prepare/dehydrate chloride feed → electrolyse to magnesium → refine → mostly return metal to titanium reduction, with some merchant ingots. MgCl2 generated in titanium production is returned for electrolysis; this is internal regeneration, not new virgin metal each cycle. The 2025 technical reference describes melting/chlorination/settling during final carnallite preparation, then metal refining and grade/melt identification for merchant ingot. This prepared-feed chain is distinct from the returned MgCl2 stream.
grade_and_analytical_basis: Prepared anhydrous carnallite: MgCl2 ≥50% (grade A) or ≥48% (B), MgO ≤0.80%, carbon ≤0.08%. These are percentages of the prepared salt, not elemental Mg or mined ore grade.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No defensible virgin-feed/primary-metal factor derived from gross plant throughput because the internal chloride loop is substantial.
supply_constraints: Electricity and external chloride makeup support an integrated titanium cycle; supplier identity and present makeup availability undisclosed.

raw_feedstock: Dolomite and ferrosilicon-based reductant; prepared feed is calcined, ground and pelletized material.
source_and_purchase_boundary: National inventory documents dolomite mining in the process chain; specific supplying quarry, contract and internal/purchased share not disclosed. Do not confuse similarly named decorative-stone businesses with this feed source.
prepared_feed_and_route: Mine/crush dolomite → calcine, grind and pelletize reduction feed → Pidgeon silicothermic reduction → refine and cast magnesium. The national inventory specifically identifies Kar Mineral and production since 2016.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No facility-specific raw or calcined feed assay or impurity limits located.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No supported t dolomite/t Mg factor located.
supply_constraints: No current documented company-specific feed disruption; mineral, reductant and energy sources remain material disclosure gaps.

producer: Ferdows magnesium project / Shemsh Felez Royal
raw_feedstock: Dolomite, ferrosilicon and fluorite; natural gas supplies process heat.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Contractor describes a domestic mineral-based project. Specific dolomite mine, grade, supply contract and reductant supplier are not disclosed.
prepared_feed_and_route: Calcine dolomite → prepare reductant-bearing briquettes → Pidgeon thermal reduction → condense/refine magnesium → ingots. Contractor documents completion in 2013 and design scope.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No plant-specific feed or prepared-charge assay located.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No consumption ratio located.
supply_constraints: A September 2026 ministry-attributed report describes the Royal/Ferdows unit as idle. The original article was inaccessible; status is retained as reported, not as an audited plant finding. Current feed availability is unknown.

raw_feedstock: Great Salt Lake brine, concentrated in company evaporation ponds; purified/dehydrated chloride is the production intermediate.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Direct lake-brine extraction and internal concentration, not purchased ore. Company describes concentration from about 0.5% Mg in lake brine to 9% Mg in pond concentrate.
prepared_feed_and_route: Concentrate brine → remove interfering constituents and prepare dry chloride → molten-salt electrolysis → refine/alloy and cast magnesium. This is the historical Rowley route; current marketing pages do not prove operation.
grade_and_analytical_basis: 0.5% and 9% are company-stated Mg concentrations, not MgO or MgCl2 percentages. A full contemporaneous impurity analysis and dry electrolyser-feed specification were not located.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: Concentration increase is not a recovery or lake-volume/metal consumption factor. No complete plant water/salt mass balance located.
supply_constraints: Falling lake levels historically drove canal extension to preserve brine access. After the 2026 state asset purchase, Utah offered the former property for mineral-extraction and processing redevelopment. Lake protection and redevelopment both matter; the offering does not establish a selected operator or magnesium restart.

raw_feedstock: Historically carnallite and internally recycled magnesium chloride from titanium production.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Historical Uralkali carnallite supply is documented in court records. Current mine/supplier terms and fresh-versus-returned chloride split are undisclosed.
prepared_feed_and_route: Prepare chloride feed → electrolyse magnesium → use magnesium in titanium-chloride reduction → recycle resulting MgCl2. Gross circulating metal is not necessarily new primary supply.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No current feed assay or prepared-electrolyte specification verified.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No valid virgin-feed-to-primary-metal ratio established.
supply_constraints: A 2026 industry bulletin reports cessation of primary smelting. This does not establish closure of the entire titanium complex or cessation of internal regeneration.

producer: Qinghai Salt Lake Magnesium / former Magontec chain
raw_feedstock: Magnesium-rich salt-lake brine/chloride intermediate; purified, dehydrated chloride feeds electrolysis.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Qarhan salt-lake resource at Golmud. Magontec bought/received primary liquid magnesium for alloy conversion; that does not make it a second primary smelter.
prepared_feed_and_route: Brine/chloride preparation → dehydration and electrolysis at the upstream complex → liquid magnesium → former Magontec alloy casthouse → alloy products. A 2025 one-cell trial separately documented chloride melting/purification before electrolysis, including MgO below 0.06% in prepared molten MgCl2. Trial performance does not establish continuous whole-site operation.
grade_and_analytical_basis: A 2025 trial reports prepared molten MgCl2 feed with MgO below 0.06%; this is an impurity in the prepared melt, not Mg content of lake brine. No current raw-brine assay or full impurity panel located.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: Trial melting/purification reports 99.12% MgCl2 recovery. This is not a fresh-brine-to-metal yield; different campaign periods prevent a defensible overall feed/product ratio.
supply_constraints: Magontec’s 2025 report records the Qinghai operation’s 2024 production cessation and entity closure in May 2025. Assets transferred to QSLM; the report alone does not prove permanent closure of all upstream electrolysis. A 2025 trial reports resolution of excess nickel in product; later commercialization still requires process scale-up.

facility: Bottrop, Germany; Sântana, Romania; Xi’an, China (anodes)
raw_feedstock: Industrial magnesium diecasting scrap; purchased primary alloy/metal; alloying additions. These are metal-bearing inputs, not virgin mineral ore.
source_and_purchase_boundary: European automotive diecasters return scrap to Bottrop/Sântana. A new, unnamed Chinese primary-alloy supplier supported 2025 distribution; no supplier identity is inferred from the phrase “world’s largest.”
prepared_feed_and_route: Collect and segregate production scrap → remelt/clean and adjust chemistry → cast reusable alloy → return to diecasters. Separately buy/distribute primary alloy and manufacture sacrificial anodes. This is recycling/alloy conversion, not new primary extraction.
grade_and_analytical_basis: Feed is alloy-dependent; lot-level Mg content, oils/oxides and acceptance limits are not disclosed. Product alloy labels are not assays of the total scrap stream.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: The 2024 report describes 40–50% of diecaster input returning as production scrap. That is a caster-loop fraction, not recycler metal loss or virgin-feed yield.
supply_constraints: Automotive casting activity controls scrap availability. Following Qinghai exit, external primary-alloy supply is needed to service customers.

raw_feedstock: Magnesium alloy production scrap and metal inputs; contract recycling streams.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Customer diecasting/industrial scrap; individual suppliers, geographic allocation and primary-metal top-up suppliers undisclosed.
prepared_feed_and_route: Sort/prepare compatible scrap → remelt and refine → adjust alloy chemistry → cast alloy ingots or return customer metal. The operation supplies secondary metal/alloys rather than extracting virgin magnesium from ore.
grade_and_analytical_basis: No representative incoming scrap Mg assay or contamination limits found; alloy designation alone is not a mixed-feed analysis.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No published scrap-in/alloy-out mass balance found.
supply_constraints: Supply depends on suitable segregated scrap and customer casting activity; a current company-specific disruption was not established.

facility: Manchester area, United Kingdom; this profile does not aggregate all global Luxfer sites
raw_feedstock: Purchased magnesium/alloying inputs and returned machining chips, swarf and turnings. Group alloy recipes use rare-earth metals including yttrium, gadolinium and neodymium; this does not identify a specific batch or supplier.
source_and_purchase_boundary: Customer machining waste and internally generated manufacturing scrap. Primary-metal smelter suppliers and exact return-stream shares undisclosed. Company identifies purpose-built Manchester recycling capability.
prepared_feed_and_route: Accept segregated machining returns → prepare/remelt compatible metal → adjust/refine alloy → cast/work material and machine finished parts → return internal scrap to recycling. No virgin ore-to-metal extraction is established at the covered operation.
grade_and_analytical_basis: Return value and acceptance depend on alloy identity and contamination; no representative incoming-feed Mg content or numerical oil/water limits verified.
consumption_ratio_and_boundary: No disclosed scrap-to-recovered-alloy mass balance or primary top-up ratio.
supply_constraints: Segregation and contaminated machining waste constrain recycling. At group level, some alloy rare-earth inputs are sourced from China; named magnesium-smelter suppliers remain unverified.
